Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the question queue will be given at that time. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Asset Management's Q3 results. Joining me on today's call are David Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Investment Officer; Robert Kline, Head of Distribution; and Emily Vargas, Head of Operations.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to David Reynolds.

David Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by resilient net inflows across our diversified franchises and favorable market appreciation in equities and alternatives. Our AUM grew to $1.45 trillion.

Michael Chen: Thank you, David. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3. Our revenue was $1.15 billion, representing a 16% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by the direct linkage between our expanding AUM base and fee income, compounded by positive flows and a favorable product mix tilting toward higher-margin areas.

Let me unpack this in detail, starting with how AUM changes fueled our top line. Our revenue model is overwhelmingly fee-based, with roughly 78% from management fees on average daily AUM, 12% from performance incentives in alternatives and active equities, and the balance from servicing and admin fees. Ending AUM hit $1.45 trillion as of September 30, up 8.2% quarter-over-quarter and 14.7% year-over-year, while average AUM for the quarter averaged $1.42 trillion. This drove management fee revenue to $920 million, up 18% year-over-year, at a blended fee rate of 42 basis points—stable despite compression in passive products, thanks to growth in alternatives averaging 95 basis points and performance fees adding $145 million from realizations in private credit and equity pods.

Market appreciation accounted for about 65% of AUM growth, contributing $52 billion from global equity beta and a $4 billion FX lift from USD strength. Net flows added $28.4 billion for the quarter, pushing year-to-date to $92.1 billion, or 6.8% of average AUM—well above our 4-6% long-term target. A 1% rise in average AUM typically adds 42 basis points to revenue at current rates, but mix shifts amplified this: passive ETFs now 42% of AUM at sub-20 bps fees, actives at 35 bps with strong outperformance, and alts providing margin uplift.

Regionally, North America at 62% of AUM grew on $18.9 billion flows from DC plans; EMEA added $5.2 billion via UCITS ETFs; APAC surged 45% YoY to $3.7 billion on joint ventures; EM contributed $0.6 billion. Equity AUM at $892 billion rose 11.3% QoQ, ETFs to $415 billion with $14.2 billion inflows, fixed income $378 billion flat but with $6.8 billion flows, alts record $210 billion up 7.9%.

Our total net flows for the period totaled $28.4 billion, with gross inflows of $62 billion against outflows of $33.6 billion, yielding a 46% net-to-gross ratio—indicating robust retention. Long-term flows hit $24.9 billion, led by equities at $16.2 billion including ETF strength, fixed income $6.8 billion, alts $4.1 billion, and money markets $3.5 billion tempered by yield compression post-Fed cuts.

By channel, institutional led with $17.6 billion or 62%, including pension mandates and OCIO wins; retail $4 billion accelerating on target-date and model portfolios via wirehouses; alternatives $6.8 billion record, private credit $3.5 billion, PE $1.7 billion, real assets $1.6 billion—fueled by evergreen structures and secondaries platforms.

Expenses totaled $285 million, up 8% year-over-year from $264 million, but our expense-to-revenue ratio improved to 62% from 63.5%, leveraging scale from 15% revenue growth. Compensation and benefits at $157 million, 55% of total, up 10% on 7% headcount growth to 2,850 in quants and multi-asset, base pay up 5%, variables $42 million on alts performance, equity awards $28 million. Tech and data $28.5 million up 25% on AWS/Snowflake scaling, Bloomberg fees, gen-AI pilots with 15% efficiency gains. Distribution/marketing $42.8 million up 2% but down as % mix on inflow scale, servicing steady. G&A $56.7 million up 5% on legal/audit for SEC exams, travel rebound.

Our expense ratio improved due to productivity from AI tools cutting research hours 20%, RPA automation, and zero-based budgeting—positioning for 60% margin expansion next year.

For guidance, Q4 net flows $25-35 billion implying FY24 $117-127 billion or 5.5-6% of average AUM; FY24-end AUM $1.55-1.60 trillion, 2025 $1.75-1.85 trillion on 4-5% organic plus 6-8% markets. Catalysts: Aladdin-integrated platform reducing alpha decay 15-20%, new active ETFs targeting $10-15 billion inflows, megatrends in retirement, privates, ESG now 35% AUM SFDR-compliant. Risks: Fed pivot outflows, EM volatility; upsides: M&A like $12 billion Horizon deal, $500 million tech plan boosting pipeline conversion 12%.

Net income came in at $420 million, reflecting these efficiencies.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities, where our active large-cap growth funds outperformed benchmarks by 210 basis points net. We are navigating the current market environment by emphasizing diversification into AI-themed ETFs, clean energy, and private infrastructure, while enhancing risk analytics via our proprietary platforms. We launched the Apex AI Equity ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $2.5 billion in inflows and strong uptake from RIAs, contributing to ETF AUM growth to 28.6% of total.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Lisa. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC are paying off, as evidenced by 45% YoY flow acceleration to $3.7 billion, driven by samurai bond strategies, QFII allocations in China, and partnerships with Japanese keiretsu—bolstered by our model delivery and AdvisorHub app boosting conversions 18%.

Emily Vargas: Thank you, Robert. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure, including cloud migrations and gen-AI for portfolio optimization, resulting in 15-20% efficiency gains and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on regtech compliance in APAC and blockchain for NAV calculations in tokenized pilots, alongside RPA for back-office savings.

David Reynolds: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes deepening product innovation like semi-transparent ETFs and interval funds, pursuing bolt-on M&A in Asia, and leveraging AI for flow forecasting and dynamic allocation to sustain 5-7% organic growth through cycles.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one-one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. Our first question comes from Alex Thompson with Morningstar.

Alex Thompson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on AUM and flow guidance for upcoming periods?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Alex. As I outlined, we're guiding Q4 net flows to $25-35 billion, full-year $117-127 billion or 5.5-6% of average AUM, assuming VIX 18-22 and stable geopolitics. AUM ends FY24 at $1.55-1.60 trillion, 2025 at $1.75-1.85 trillion on organic 4-5% plus market tailwinds. Key drivers: Aladdin platform rollout for OCIO wins, Q1 '25 ETF launches targeting $10-15 billion, retirement solutions, private markets scaling to $45 billion AUA with 22% fee earnings growth, ESG at 35% compliant. Fee discipline offsets 2 bps compression, with alts at 95 bps and $1.2 billion YTD performance fees. Upside from Horizon M&A and tech investments; risks from Fed dovishness or EM tariffs.

Alex Thompson: Thank you. And a follow-up on operating expenses?

Michael Chen: On op ex, the $285 million total rose 8% YoY on talent/tech investments supporting $1.45 trillion AUM, but ratio improved to 62% via leverage. Comp $157 million up 10% on headcount/tech hires; tech $28.5 million +25% on AI/cloud; distribution $42.8 million scale-efficient; G&A $56.7 million on compliance. H2 mid-single growth moderated by AI productivity, targeting 10% savings in 2025 for margin expansion.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jennifer Lee with Bloomberg.

Jennifer Lee: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of our flagship equity funds?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Jennifer. Our equities franchise at $892 billion shone, up 11.3% QoQ with S&P outperformance. Flagship Apex Growth Equity Fund beat by 210 bps net, driven by AI/semiconductor tilts amid tech rally. 68% of active equity funds beat 3-year benchmarks, supporting institutional stickiness alongside ETF growth.

Jennifer Lee: And how is the new product Apex AI Equity ETF performing relative to expectations?

Robert Kline: It's exceeding, Jennifer, with $2.5 billion inflows already versus $1.5 billion target, strong RIA/wirehouse adoption on Schwab/Fidelity. Early AUM momentum positions it for $10 billion+ run-rate, enhancing our 42% passive share.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Rivera with Goldman Sachs.

Mark Rivera: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Emily Vargas: Absolutely, Mark. Tech infra upgrades like gen-AI pilots and Aladdin integration cut operational alpha decay 15-20%, analyst hours 20%, trade reconciliation efficiency up 15%. Blockchain NAV and RPA target further 10% savings, reducing risk while supporting tokenized pilots and APAC regtech.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to David Reynolds for closing remarks.

David Reynolds: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
